name: pRFLife with mrTools
summary: Estimates voxel-wise population receptive fields (polar angle, eccentricity, size, R2) from retinotopy fMRI and its stimulus with the mrTools pRF model.
description: Fits the mrTools pRF model to each voxel of the fMRI time series given the stimulus aperture. Voxels are restricted to the provided mask or, if none, to the FreeSurfer cortical ribbon in the selected lobes (occipital by default). fMRI can optionally be slice-time and motion corrected and globally regressed. The stimulus must match the fMRI timing.

inputs.description: Stimulus aperture as a pixelsX x pixelsY x time NIfTI with values in [0,1].
inputs.requirements: Must match the temporal dimension (TR) of the fMRI.

inputs.description: FreeSurfer subject directory, used to build the cortical mask and surfaces.
Optional mask in fMRI space restricting the voxels analysed (for example V1).

outputs.description: pRF maps (r2, polar angle, eccentricity, receptive field size) as NIfTI, plus surface VTKs.

parameters.description: Perform slice timing and head motion correction on fMRI before running prf
Repetition time of fMRI (read from the nii header if unspecified)
Width in degrees subtended of visual stimulus (16° for HCP)
Height in degrees subtended of visual stimulus (16° for HCP)
Specifies whether global signal regression (GSR) on input fMRI should be done, conversion to % change from baseline

options.label: per-voxel normalization
options.description: regresses out mean signal per voxel

parameters.description: Only do the grid search that finds approximately good parameters for the model and will not optimize with the nonlinear search. This will speed up the program but will not produce optimized fits.

citations.text: Gardner JL, Merriam EP, Schluppeck D, Besle J, Heeger DJ. mrTools: Analysis and visualization package for functional magnetic resonance imaging data (Version 4.7). Zenodo (2018).

failure_modes.cause: prf/r2.nii.gz was not produced by the pRF fit.
failure_modes.fix: Check the fMRI, stimulus and mask inputs and the MATLAB log.
